chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn A'idh al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Wajna al-Nasibi, who said:
I heard Abu Naeem Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ansari… and he mentioned the like of it.

key_terms.أَبُو نَعِيمٍ: Abu Naeem, a title for Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ansari
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الرَّازِيُّ: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, a narrator
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ وَجْنَاءَ النَّصِيبِيِّ: Al-Hasan ibn Wajna al-Nasibi, a narrator
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَائِذٍ: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn A'idh al-Razi, a narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ansari, a narrator

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for the report on the birth of the Master of the Age in Tusi's Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a secondary chain (isnad) corroborating the report of the Imam’s birth, highlighting the rigorous transmission methods used to establish the Occultation's historical basis. By citing al-Hasan ibn Wajna, a prominent companion of the Imams, al-Tusi reinforces the authenticity of the event within the Shia scholarly tradition, linking the physical birth to the divine plan of preservation.
